newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-CHANDERPAUL HITS MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CHANDERPAUL HITS MAIDEN TEST CENTURY.

text.p: Shivnarine Chanderpaul hit his maiden test century to keep the West Indies alive on the first day of the third test match against India on Thursday.

Chanderpaul's disciplined innings helped the West Indies survive the first day after the Indian bowlers had them on the ropes, with pacemen Venkatesh Prasad and Dodda Ganesh reducing them to 144 for five by tea.

Prasad, who bowled an immaculate off-stump line and got the ball to bounce and swing, was the pick of the bowlers, capturing four for 58 off 25 overs during the day. Ganesh took two for 70 off 21 overs in his first game of the series.

Chanderpaul, who at one stage looked like he could be deprived his centry by a lack of batting parters, calmly batted on as the wickets fell around him, helping West Indies reach a more respecable 240 for seven at the close.

"It is a big relief and I am happy, too. It's been a long wait and a heavy load on my shoulders," said Chanderpaul, who was mobbed by around 300 fans who ran onto the pitch when he passed the 100 mark.
At the close, Chanderpaul was 102 not out, with Curtly Ambrose unbeaten on 28.
Chanderpaul, playing his 19th test and batting his 30th innings, entered the fray in the third over after opener Sherwin Campbell was removed by Prasad for six with the score on 10.

Despite starting uncertainly and having a slice of luck at 62, when he was dropped by wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia off leg- spinner Anil Kumble, Chanderpaul, who has 13 test half centuries, batted with dedication and determination.
His team-mates struggled to come to terms with a bouncy pitch and Chanderpaul was the only West Indian batsman to pass 30.
Chanderpaul lost his first partner when opener Stuart Williams was bowled by Ganesh for 24 as the West Indies reached 68 for two by lunch.
Prasad captured the prized wicket of stand-in captain Brian Lara with a beautiful out-swinger which the batsman edged to captain Sachin Tendulkar at first slip for 19..
Carl Hooper was next to go, also for 19. He flashed at a wide delivery from Ganesh and edged a catch to Mongia.
Roland Holder, playing his first test before his home fans, did not last long. He was caught at third slip by Mohammad Azharuddin off Prasad for five.

In the final session, Chanderpaul and wicket-keeper Courtney Browne added 56 runs for the sixth wicket before Anil Kumble, the series leading wicket-taker with 15 scalps in the first two tests, separated them.
Browne skied a catch to Tendulkar, running back from a short mid-wicket and was out for 24. Six runs later, Ian Bishop was bowled by Prasad for four.
He was replaced by Ambrose who gave Chanderpaul admirable support as he inched towards his century which finally came when he drove Ganesh through the vacant mid-on for three.
Chanderpaul faced 231 balls and hit eight fours in his innings.
